(i).text: More generally, at every certified evaluation behind the tables of Section~\ref{sec:results}, every penalised slack in $Q$ (daily closure and network feasibility) sits at its zero bound to within the solver's bound relaxation, so no penalty is paid in $Q$, and the agent's net-power pair, penalised in the agent's own objective, is at its bound as well; the relaxation itself leaves a common offset of $-13.0$~k\euro{} in $Q$ ($-2 \times 10^{-5}$ of $Q$), identical across evaluations to within 40~\euro{}, which cancels in every reported difference. The multi-scenario evaluation of the reference unit carries a positive flexibility-balance content of at most 2.2~\euro{}, and the superseded evaluation~16 a positive slack content of at most 171~\euro{}, almost all of it voltage slack.

(ii).rule: W188 (d) contact rule: within 1e-4 MWh of the limit (n_contact_* columns of soc_block_summary_reference_unit.csv, the TSO copy, as W189 part 1)
(ii).text: Figure~\ref{fig:res_soc_soh} shows how degradation reaches the dispatch. Panel~(a) gives the stored energy of the reference unit over the four representative days of 2025 and 2035 under the baseline calibration: the unit cycles once or twice a day across the usable band, reaching the 90\,\% limit of its available energy on every day and the 10\,\% limit on six of the eight (the Winter days stop at 14--15\,\%), and in 2035, with the state of health at the 0.70 floor, the usable band has narrowed from 0.70 to 0.56~MWh. Panel~(b) gives the end-of-block state of health under the seven calibrations: the baseline and both 50\,\% retention calibrations reach the floor in the 2035 block, the cycling-only and datasheet calibrations do not, and the 0.50 floor lets the baseline calibration continue to 0.68.
